newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Chrysler sets up SE Asia office in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler sets up SE Asia office in Singapore.

text.p: American car maker Chrysler Corp is opening a Southeast Asian headquarters in Singapore to oversee regional expansion, Michael Morton, managing director of Chrysler Southeast Asia Pte Ltd, said on Thursday.
He also announced that Chrysler had established a dealership in Singapore with Komoco Auto Pte Ltd, a company controlled by businessman Ong Beng Seng and distributor of South Korea's Hyundai cars.
Sales of Chrysler vehicles in Southeast Asia rose 30 percent in 1995 over 1994 and are now worth about US$250 million a year, he said.
Chrysler sold about 10,000 vehicles, of which 6,000 are domestically assembled in Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia.
"Thailand is current the largest market accounting for 65-70 percent of sales in the region," said Morton.
He said other major regional markets were Malaysia and Indonesia and there were plans to increase production in these markets, but plans had not been finalised.
Morton said Chrysler also saw good potential in emerging markets like Philippines, India, Vietnam and Cambodia.
Chrysler already has a dealer in the Philippines but it was planning to find a distributor there and expand the number of dealers, said Morton.
In Singapore, he said Chrysler planned to introduced five models, including the Grand Cherokee and the Voyager by November.
Morton said details on pricing and sales volume for Singapore were still being negotiated with Komoco.
